newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court raps far right for theatre rampage.
newsitem.headline: French court raps far right for theatre rampage.

text.p: A French court on Tuesday slapped suspended prison sentences on five members of the far-right National Front for obstructing freedom of expression and banned two of them from holding office after they attacked a theatre company.

Ex-Lyon mayor Michel Noir had filed charges against the five men after they stormed on stage and assaulted actors during a premier of Anton Checkov's "Uncle Vanya" last November in which he was playing a star role.

Denis de Bouteiller, head of the Front's southeastern Rhone branch, and Philippe Dumez, a member of the Lyon city council, were among 30 party members who had barged into the Lyon theatre carrying banners reading "Noir the Thief", throwing objects, and blowing horns.
They reproached Noir for having refused to rent out a meeting hall for a Front rally when he was mayor.
Both men were banned from holding public office for a year.
"There has been a violation of free expression...in a democracy growing increasingly fragile toward the end of the century," the court said in its ruling.
"It cannot be accepted that leaders and elected officials from the National Front consider themselves censors of culture and flout free expression through commando actions," it added.
Bruno Gollnisch, number three to anti-immigrant party leader Jean-Marie Le Pen, had acted as his colleagues' lawyer during the trial.

Noir, a former member of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR who served as trade minister in the 1980s, decided to try his hand at acting after resigning as mayor and member of parliament over his involvement in a political corruption scandal.
He was given an 18-month suspended sentence in the affair.
